summary: Implementation-level knowledge from CLAUDE.md (data flows, Food Inspector, weekly plans, email, agent and chatui internals). Only facts not already proposed from the root README (proposal 01).

ops.text: There is no top-level package manager tying the three services together; each has its own `requirements.txt` (Python, pinned) or `package.json` (Node).
ops.quote: There is no top-level package manager tying the three together

ops.text: The only genuinely cross-service code is `shared/constants.py` (day / meal-type vocabulary and ordering).
ops.quote: The one piece of genuinely cross-service code is `shared/constants.py`

ops.text: All three services require `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY` to be set and refuse to start without it.
ops.quote: all three refuse to start without it

ops.text: `docker-compose.yml` fails fast via `${KITCHENHQ_API_KEY:?...}` if `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY` is missing from the root `.env`.
ops.quote: fails fast via `${KITCHENHQ_API_KEY:?...}` if it's missing

ops.text: Every dbmcp request (REST and MCP) needs an `X-API-Key: <KITCHENHQ_API_KEY>` header.
ops.quote: Every request (REST and MCP) needs an `X-API-Key: <KITCHENHQ_API_KEY>` header

ops.text: A 401 from any chatui `/api/*` call clears the stored key in the browser and re-prompts for it.
ops.quote: a 401 from any `/api/*` call clears it and re-prompts

ops.text: chatui's own `/api/*` routes (except `/api/health`) sit behind the same `require_api_key` middleware pattern as dbmcp, since real users hit them directly from the browser.
ops.quote: since real users hit them directly from the browser

ops.text: The chatui React app has a key-entry gate (`src/components/AccessGate.jsx`) in front of everything else in `App.jsx`; `src/services/api.js` attaches the stored key to every request and clears it on a 401.
ops.quote: `src/components/AccessGate.jsx`

ops.text: `KITCHEN_DB_HOST_PATH` in the root `.env` relocates the SQLite volume (defaults to `./data`).
ops.quote: Set `KITCHEN_DB_HOST_PATH` in root `.env` to relocate the SQLite volume (defaults to `./data`)

ops.text: `KITCHEN_TIMEZONE` sets the scheduler's `TZ` (default `Asia/Kolkata`).
ops.quote: `KITCHEN_TIMEZONE` sets the scheduler's `TZ`

ops.text: agent-api requires dbmcp reachable at `MCP_URL` (default `http://localhost:18000/mcp` outside Docker; the Docker Compose network uses the service name `dbmcp`) and a `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY` matching dbmcp's.
ops.quote: Requires `dbmcp` reachable at `MCP_URL`

ops.text: chatui's `AGENT_API_URL` and `DB_API_URL` default to the Docker service names (`AGENT_API_URL` default `http://agent-api:8090`).
ops.quote: AGENT_API_URL/DB_API_URL default to the Docker service names

ops.text: The MCP app is served via `mcp.streamable_http_app()` mounted on the same FastAPI app as the REST routes.
ops.quote: via `mcp.streamable_http_app()` mounted on the same FastAPI app

ops.text: `kitchendb/schema.py`'s `initialize_database()` runs `schema.sql` and seeds a fresh DB (`kitchendb/seed.py`); it is called on FastAPI `lifespan` startup.
ops.quote: `initialize_database()` runs that script and seeds a fresh DB

ops.text: Data operations in `kitchendb/tools/*.py` are decorated with a local `@tool`; `kitchendb/tools/registry.py` collects them and `kitchendb/server.py`'s `build_mcp()` adds each to a fresh `FastMCP` instance built per app.
ops.quote: `kitchendb/server.py`'s `build_mcp()` adds each one to a fresh `FastMCP` instance built per app

ops.text: `kitchendb/routes.py` re-exposes almost every tool as a thin Pydantic-validated FastAPI REST route that calls the same function.
ops.quote: re-exposes almost every one of them as a thin Pydantic-validated FastAPI REST route

ops.text: `dbmcp/init_db.py` is only a compatibility shim (`uvicorn init_db:app`, the `python init_db.py` dev runner) re-exporting from the `kitchendb` package; the implementation is not in that file.
ops.quote: is now only a compatibility shim

ops.text: When extending inventory-affecting flows, preserve idempotency (not the exact response shape).
ops.quote: Preserve idempotency (not the exact response shape) when extending inventory-affecting flows

ops.text: Idempotency keys for inventory-affecting acknowledgements are recorded in `inventory_transactions.idempotency_key`.
ops.quote: recorded in `inventory_transactions.idempotency_key`

ops.text: Shopping's `acknowledge_shopping_items` returns `{"replayed": True, ...}` on a repeat call, whereas prep's `capture_prep_completion_status` returns the unchanged row with no `replayed` flag, so a prep replay is recognised by `status`.
ops.quote: check `status`, not a `replayed` key

ops.text: `add_detailed_prep_schedule(detailed_instructions: list[str], ingredients_used: list[{item_name, quantity, unit}])` stores both as validated JSON on the row with `status='assigned'` and `created_at` stamped.
ops.quote: stores both as validated JSON on the row (`status='assigned'`, `created_at` stamped)

ops.text: `ingredients_used` is the only place the agent supplies what a prep task will consume; it is matched by `item_name`, never `inventory_id`, since the caller cannot reliably know an id ahead of time.
ops.quote: matched by `item_name`, never `inventory_id`

ops.text: Prep has no separate acknowledge endpoint: `capture_prep_completion_status(is_completed=True)` is the one human action ("check this task off") and always deducts whatever `ingredients_used` holds.
ops.quote: There is no separate acknowledge endpoint or step for prep

ops.text: A prep task with empty `ingredients_used` becomes `status='completed'` when checked off (nothing to deduct, so it can still be reopened).
ops.quote: empty → `status='completed'`

ops.text: A prep task with non-empty `ingredients_used` becomes `status='acknowledged'` when checked off (key `prep-<id>-complete`) and is locked against reopening, because undoing a real deduction is not safe to automate.
ops.quote: non-empty → `status='acknowledged'`

ops.text: Both `completed` and `acknowledged` mean "done" to the household and land in the same "recently completed" bucket (dashboard, `get_prep_schedules`, chatui's Task List); an `acknowledged` row rejects a later `is_completed=False` call with 400 while a `completed` one does not.
ops.quote: an `acknowledged` row rejects a later `is_completed=False` call (400)

ops.text: `inventory.quantity` and `inventory_transactions.quantity_after` have no `>= 0` CHECK in `schema.sql`.
ops.quote: have no `>= 0` CHECK in `schema.sql`

ops.text: A prep task still `'assigned'` more than 2 hours after `created_at` is stale; `expire_stale_prep_tasks()` (MCP tool, no REST route) flips it to `status='expired'` without touching inventory.
ops.quote: flips it to `status='expired'` — never touching inventory

ops.text: `capture_prep_completion_status` and `cancel_prep_schedule` reject an expired prep task with 400, as they do an already-`acknowledged` row.
ops.quote: then reject it (400)

ops.text: The `expire_prep_tasks` job is the only caller of `expire_stale_prep_tasks()`; it is a deterministic housekeeping sweep, not a planning decision.
ops.quote: it's a deterministic housekeeping sweep, not a planning decision

ops.text: `shopping_items.item_name` is unique with `COLLATE NOCASE`.
ops.quote: unique on `item_name` (`COLLATE NOCASE`)

ops.text: `add_shopping_items` is an `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(item_name) DO UPDATE` upsert that merges `proposed_quantity`, so callers never choose between creating and appending.
ops.quote: merges `proposed_quantity`

ops.text: `edit_shopping_item`, `delete_shopping_item` and `clear_shopping_items` round out add/edit/delete/clear for the shopping list.
ops.quote: round out add/edit/delete/clear

ops.text: `acknowledge_shopping_items` is REST-only (not an MCP tool) because it is a human action, not an agent one; it matches each purchased item to `inventory` by `item_name`.
ops.quote: REST-only, not an MCP tool

ops.text: Because the `shopping_items` row is gone on replay, shopping acknowledgement idempotency is checked against `inventory_transactions.idempotency_key` (`{acknowledgement_key}:{shopping_item_id}`) instead of a status flag.
ops.quote: idempotency is checked directly against `inventory_transactions.idempotency_key`

ops.text: `household_members` holds individual household members (`id`, `name`, `dietary_preferences` JSON array, `health_conditions` JSON array).
ops.quote: `household_members` (`id`, `name`, `dietary_preferences` JSON array, `health_conditions` JSON array)

ops.text: `household_members` CRUD is REST-only (`/api/household-members`), edited by a human on the Profile page rather than through an agent tool, and the rows are embedded in `GET /api/dashboard` as `household_members`.
ops.quote: CRUD is REST-only (`/api/household-members`

ops.text: `user_profile.restrictions` is a JSON list of `{id, label, category, enabled, scope, value?}` where `scope` is `"per_meal"` or `"week"`.
ops.quote: JSON list of `{id, label, category, enabled, scope, value?}`

ops.text: `user_profile` holds the booleans `allow_recipe_invention` and `allow_unapproved_recipes`; the latter is captured but unused until a recipe-approval workflow exists.
ops.quote: captured but unused until a recipe-approval workflow exists

ops.text: `user_profile.skip_meals` is JSON `{day_of_week: [meal_type, ...]}` listing slots to leave unplanned for the coming week.
ops.quote: slots to leave unplanned for the coming week

ops.text: `user_profile.preferred_tags` and `excluded_tags` are JSON string arrays drawn from the categorized taxonomy in `shared/tags.py` (cuisine / dietary / allergen / religious / method), a suggested vocabulary rather than an enforced enum.
ops.quote: a suggested vocabulary, not an enforced enum

ops.text: `shared/tags.py` is vendored the same way as `shared/constants.py` and exposed to chatui via `GET /api/dashboard`'s `constants.tags`.
ops.quote: exposed to chatui via `GET /api/dashboard`'s `constants.tags`

ops.text: `user_profile.favorite_recipes` is a legacy JSON field (max 10, newest first) that nothing currently writes to, since the star-rating flow that populated it was removed in favour of `household_members`.
ops.quote: a legacy field nothing currently writes to

ops.text: Example restrictions: `no_nonveg_lunch` (`per_meal`; the old egg/meat/fish rule) and `lunch_variety` (`week` scope with a `value` parameter, its minimum distinct count; the old five-distinct-lunches rule).
ops.quote: `no_nonveg_lunch`, the old egg/meat/fish rule

ops.text: The `get_household_preferences` MCP tool folds household members, restrictions, tags, skip meals, the free-text chef note (`user_profile.notes`) and `favorite_recipes` together, plus a `has_preferences` bool and a `guidance` line.
ops.quote: plus a `has_preferences` bool and a `guidance` line

ops.text: `get_household_preferences` is the single shared source of household rules, preferences, conditions and restrictions: the Executive Chef and Sous Chef prompts tell them to consult it before deciding what to cook, and the Food Inspector consults the same tool when auditing, never a duplicated rules file.
ops.quote: never a duplicated rules file

ops.text: Household preferences are optional context: when `get_household_preferences` comes back empty (`has_preferences: false`, as on a fresh install) every role proceeds anyway.
ops.quote: every role proceeds anyway

ops.text: `restrictions` is excluded from the empty-preferences check because it always carries its two seeded defaults.
ops.quote: since it always carries its two seeded defaults

ops.text: The `weekly_menu` job builds a week slot by slot with 28 `add_weekly_menu_item` upserts (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(day_of_week, meal_type) DO UPDATE`), guarded by the `UNIQUE` index on `(day_of_week, meal_type)` in `schema.sql`.
ops.quote: guarded by the `UNIQUE` index on `(day_of_week, meal_type)` in `schema.sql`

ops.text: `add_weekly_menu_item` takes `ingredients: list[str]` and `full_recipe: list[str]` as plain-text lines stored as JSON arrays (UI and emails render them as `<ul>`/`<ol>`; `parse_lines` handles legacy string rows).
ops.quote: plain-text lines, stored as JSON arrays

ops.text: `add_weekly_menu_item` requires a `description`, a short household-facing summary shown on the Weekly Menu page's meal card in place of a raw ingredient/macro preview.
ops.quote: a required `description`

ops.text: `add_weekly_menu_item` accepts an optional `tags` list (same freeform taxonomy as a `recipes` catalog entry's tags).
ops.quote: an optional `tags` list

ops.text: `add_weekly_menu_item` accepts an optional `source_recipe_id`, the `recipes` catalog id the dish was adapted from via `search_recipes`, which tells a later "recreate instructions"/"identify tags" request whether the catalog recipe or the `weekly_menu` row is the authoritative record to edit.
ops.quote: an optional `source_recipe_id`

ops.text: `add_weekly_menu_item` refreshes the row's `updated_at` on every upsert.
ops.quote: refreshes the row's `updated_at` on every upsert

ops.text: The old whole-week `add_weekly_menu_plan` function and its `POST /api/weekly-menu/{plan,validate}` routes were removed entirely in the `dbmcp` reorg, leaving only the per-slot `add_weekly_menu_item` upsert (`POST /api/weekly-menu`).
ops.quote: are gone entirely

ops.text: `weekly_menu` slots excluded by `skip_meals` are saved as placeholders with `dish_name='Skipped'` and `is_skipped=1`.
ops.quote: `dish_name='Skipped'`, `is_skipped=1` placeholder

ops.text: Skipped placeholders are pre-scored `score=100` so they never surface in `get_unaudited_weekly_menu_items`.
ops.quote: pre-scored (`score=100`)

ops.text: `add_weekly_menu_item` clears `is_skipped` back to 0 (and resets `score`/`audit_feedback` to `NULL`) whenever a real dish is saved for that slot again.
ops.quote: clears `is_skipped` back to `0`

ops.text: `weekly_plans` is the whole-week counterpart to `weekly_menu`'s per-slot rows: one row per planned week (`week_start_date`/`week_end_date`, unique on `week_start_date`).
ops.quote: one row per planned week

ops.text: Each `weekly_plans` row holds `skip_meals_snapshot`, `chef_note_snapshot` and `restrictions_snapshot` (copies of `user_profile.skip_meals`/`notes`/`restrictions`, the last filtered to `enabled: true`) as they were when that week was planned, plus its own `score`/`audit_feedback`.
ops.quote: *at the moment that week was planned*

ops.text: `weekly_plan_audit` is a deliberate exception among the audits: it judges against the snapshot taken at plan time, whereas `weekly_menu`, `detailed_prep_schedule` and `recipes` audits judge against the household's current rules.
ops.quote: This is a deliberate exception to the rest of this schema's audits

ops.text: A `weekly_plans` row is created deterministically, not by an agent tool call: after a successful `weekly_menu` job, `run_job` computes the week's start/end dates from `get_job_context`'s `target_menu_days` and posts them with the planning snapshot to `POST /api/weekly-plans`.
ops.quote: created **deterministically, not by an agent tool call**

ops.text: `POST /api/weekly-plans` is REST-only (`kitchendb/tools/weekly_plan.py::upsert_weekly_plan`) and follows the same "code posts after job completion" pattern as `agent_runs` telemetry, so an LLM cannot forget the step.
ops.quote: so an LLM can't forget the step

ops.text: The planning snapshot (`skip_meals`/`notes`/enabled `restrictions`) is fetched once before the job runs by `_fetch_planning_snapshot` in `agents/app/jobs.py`.
ops.quote: fetched once before the job runs

ops.text: `weekly_plan.py::parse_weekly_plan_row` turns `skip_meals_snapshot`/`restrictions_snapshot` back into native JSON for every reader (`get_weekly_plans`, `get_unaudited_weekly_plans`, `record_weekly_plan_audit`, the dashboard payload).
ops.quote: back into native JSON (object/list) for every reader

ops.text: chatui's Weekly Menu page renders all three snapshot fields alongside the plan's score.
ops.quote: renders all three snapshot fields alongside the plan's score

ops.text: Recipe tools `add_recipe`, `update_recipe`, `get_recipe`, `list_recipes`, `delete_recipe`, `rate_recipe`, `search_recipes` and `reindex_recipes` live in `dbmcp/kitchendb/tools/recipes.py` and store one JSON-structured recipe, its embedding vector and a household star rating on the same row.
ops.quote: store one JSON-structured recipe, its embedding vector, and a household star rating on the *same row*

ops.text: `reindex_recipes` is only a bulk-backfill / embedding-model-upgrade sweep, not the normal write path.
ops.quote: only a bulk-backfill/embedding-model-upgrade sweep

ops.text: `search_recipes` combines keyword search (`kitchendb/keyword_search.py`, FTS-style field scoring) and semantic search (`kitchendb/embeddings.py`, cosine top-k).
ops.quote: FTS-style field scoring

ops.text: A recipe surfaces in `search_recipes` if either its keyword or semantic score clears `_MATCH_THRESHOLD` (0.65).
ops.quote: if *either* score clears `_MATCH_THRESHOLD` (0.65)

ops.text: `weekly_menu`, `weekly_plans`, `detailed_prep_schedule` and `recipes` each carry `score` (0-100) and `audit_feedback` (text) columns; `NULL` means not yet audited.
ops.quote: `NULL` means not yet audited

ops.text: `add_weekly_menu_item` resets a slot's `score`/`audit_feedback` to `NULL` on every upsert, because a re-planned slot is a new decision awaiting judgement.
ops.quote: resets a slot's `score`/`audit_feedback` to `NULL` on every upsert

ops.text: `detailed_prep_schedule` and `recipes` rows are audited once at creation/last edit and are not reset on read.
ops.quote: audited once at creation/last edit and not reset on read

ops.text: Four MCP tool pairs drive the Food Inspector: `get_unaudited_weekly_menu_items`/`record_weekly_menu_audit`, `get_unaudited_weekly_plans`/`record_weekly_plan_audit`, `get_unaudited_prep_tasks`/`record_prep_task_audit` and `get_unaudited_recipes`/`record_recipe_audit`, all filtered on `score IS NULL`.
ops.quote: all filtered on `score IS NULL`

ops.text: The prep-task audit pair deliberately includes cancelled tasks, since the decision being judged is what the Sous Chef planned, not whether it was performed; `get_prep_schedules` by contrast excludes them.
ops.quote: deliberately **includes cancelled tasks**

ops.text: `recipes` is a household-editable catalog, not a fifth planning role's output.
ops.quote: a household-editable catalog, not a fifth planning role's output

ops.text: The four audit jobs `menu_audit`, `weekly_plan_audit`, `task_audit` and `recipe_audit` are defined in `agents/app/jobs.py` with role `food_inspector`; each fetches whatever is unaudited and scores it.
ops.quote: each fetch whatever is unaudited and score it

ops.text: `menu_audit`, `weekly_plan_audit` and `task_audit` judge against the same `system.md` rules and `get_household_preferences` context the author used, whereas `recipe_audit` uses catalog-only standards and deliberately does not call `get_household_preferences`, since a catalog recipe is not scoped to one household.
ops.quote: since a catalog recipe isn't scoped to one household

ops.text: `weekly_plan_audit` judges each row against its own snapshot rather than a fresh `get_household_preferences` call.
ops.quote: judges each row against its **own** snapshot

ops.text: `weekly_plan_audit` checks completeness: every `(day, meal_type)` slot not listed in `skip_meals_snapshot` must have a saved `weekly_menu` row for that week, and a missing one is a hard fault.
ops.quote: a missing one is a hard fault

ops.text: `weekly_plan_audit` also checks the `"week"`-scope entries of `restrictions_snapshot` (e.g. `lunch_variety`) and whether the week's dishes reflect `chef_note_snapshot` when it is non-empty.
ops.quote: whether the week's dishes reflect `chef_note_snapshot` when it's non-empty

ops.text: New jobs need no explicit Automations wiring: agent-api's `/jobs` lists `SCHEDULED_REQUESTS` dynamically and chatui's `/api/automations/*` proxies whatever it returns.
ops.quote: lists `SCHEDULED_REQUESTS` dynamically

ops.text: `food_inspector` has its own prompt fragment (`agents/prompts/food_inspector.md`) but shares `system.md` verbatim like every role.
ops.quote: shares `system.md` verbatim

ops.text: The Food Inspector's `FoodInspectorResult` is passed explicitly via `JOB_RESULT_MODELS`, the same way `weekly_menu`'s `ExecutiveChefResult` is, and is not registered in `RESPONSE_FORMATS`.
ops.quote: not registered in `RESPONSE_FORMATS`

ops.text: Only the "did you check" step of an audit job is a hard `require_tools` requirement (`get_unaudited_weekly_menu_items` / `get_unaudited_weekly_plans` / `get_unaudited_prep_tasks` / `get_unaudited_recipes`); how many rows get scored is not enforced by `JOB_REQUIRED_TOOL_COUNTS`.
ops.quote: isn't enforced by `JOB_REQUIRED_TOOL_COUNTS`

ops.text: `run_agent` enforces the full Monday-Sunday week for the `weekly_menu` job via `_weekly_menu_slot_shortfall`, which checks the distinct `(day, meal)` args actually saved, not just the call count.
ops.quote: checks the **distinct** `(day, meal)` args actually saved

ops.text: A `weekly_menu` run that re-saved weekday slots to reach 28 calls while leaving Saturday/Sunday stale is nudged and then fails.
ops.quote: leaving Saturday/Sunday stale is nudged and then fails

ops.text: Before the agent runs, `run_job` deterministically writes the `Skipped` placeholder for every slot excluded by `skip_meals` via `kitchendb/tools/weekly_menu.py::mark_weekly_menu_skipped` (REST-only, `POST /api/weekly-menu/skip`).
ops.quote: deterministically writes a `dish_name='Skipped'`

ops.text: The skip placeholders are written up front, before the agent's own `send_weekly_plan_email` call reads the saved menu back, so a slot skipped this week does not keep showing a stale dish from an earlier week in chatui and the plan email.
ops.quote: would keep showing that stale dish in both chatui and the plan email

ops.text: The Executive Chef calls `search_recipes` before inventing a dish, adapting a match rather than inventing unaided, unless `get_household_preferences.allow_recipe_invention` is false and nothing relevant comes back.
ops.quote: adapting a match rather than inventing unaided

ops.text: The Executive Chef transcribes a household member's pasted recipe into the structured shape via `add_recipe`.
ops.quote: transcribes a household member's pasted recipe

ops.text: chatui's Recipes page ("refresh tags" / "rewrite instructions") acts on a recipe catalog id via `get_recipe`/`update_recipe`.
ops.quote: on a *recipe catalog* id

ops.text: The Weekly Menu page's recipe modal makes the same kind of request against a `weekly_menu` row, touching `add_weekly_menu_item` and, when that slot has a `source_recipe_id`, the linked catalog recipe too, to keep both copies in sync.
ops.quote: to keep both copies in sync

ops.text: Both one-off recipe UI requests can pass the Food Inspector's last `score`/`audit_feedback` for that id as extra context, so the rewrite addresses the specific flagged issue.
ops.quote: instead of a generic pass

ops.text: Email lives entirely in agent-api: dbmcp has no SMTP config, no `send_*_email` tools and no `/api/notifications/*` routes.
ops.quote: `dbmcp` has no SMTP config

ops.text: `agents/app/email/` has one responsibility per module: `schemas`, `smtp`, `render`, `backfill` and `tools`.
ops.quote: one-responsibility-per-module package

ops.text: The `schemas` module holds Pydantic `*Request` payload contracts and day/meal vocabulary.
ops.quote: Pydantic `*Request` payload contracts

ops.text: The `smtp` module handles transport and recipient resolution, reading `user_profile` over `GET {DB_API_URL}/api/profile`, never SQLite.
ops.quote: never SQLite

ops.text: Each `render` builder returns `(subject, text_body, html_body)`; `parse_lines` turns a `weekly_menu` JSON-array field or legacy string into a line list.
ops.quote: each builder returns `(subject, text_body, html_body)`

ops.text: The `backfill` module fetches the saved menu from `GET /api/dashboard` for `send_weekly_plan_email` when `days` is omitted, the only email data-read left besides the recipient.
ops.quote: the only email data-read left besides the recipient

ops.text: `make_email_tools(settings)` in the `tools` module returns the three `StructuredTool`s `send_prep_task_email`, `send_weekly_plan_email` and `send_shopping_list_email`.
ops.quote: the three `StructuredTool`s

ops.text: `kitchen_agent.run_agent` appends the email tools to every run's toolset right after `get_job_context`, with the same per-request lifetime.
ops.quote: appends them to every run's toolset right after `get_job_context`

ops.text: Each email tool returns `{"sent": bool, "skipped"?: str, ...}` and never raises: a disabled `notify_on_task_creation`, an unset `SMTP_HOST` or an SMTP failure all come back as `{"sent": false}`.
ops.quote: and never raises

ops.text: An invalid email payload is rejected, and `send_shopping_list_email` rejects an empty `items`.
ops.quote: rejects an empty `items`

ops.text: Only `send_weekly_plan_email`'s `days` is optional (back-filled from the saved menu), since that email summarizes a whole week and sending it is not an enforced job step.
ops.quote: Only `send_weekly_plan_email`'s `days` is optional

ops.text: The prep and shopping-list emails take the plan/list the agent just authored and only render and send it.
ops.quote: only render + send it

ops.text: Recipient resolution (`user_profile` `email`/`cc_emails`/opt-out) stays in `smtp` server-side; the model never picks the address.
ops.quote: the model never picks the address

ops.text: `SMTP_*` environment variables are set on the `agent-api` compose service.
ops.quote: `SMTP_*` env is on the `agent-api` compose service

ops.text: The role prompts and `app/jobs.py` job prompts tell each role to send the matching email whenever it saves a prep schedule, weekly plan or shopping list.
ops.quote: tell each role to send the matching email

ops.text: `agents/app/` replaces the old single `agent.py` file.
ops.quote: replaces the old single `agent.py` god-file

ops.text: `app/kitchen_agent.run_agent(role, text, settings, ...)` is the core entry point: for each call it builds a fresh LLM client (`app/llm.build_model`) and a fresh MCP tool set (`app/mcp_tools.load_tools`), runs the LangChain agent, and disposes the LLM client's HTTP connections (`app/llm.dispose_model`) in a `finally` block.
ops.quote: for *this call only*

ops.text: `run_agent` returns the model's `structured_response` JSON when a `response_format` is in play, else the final assistant text via `_final_text()` (last non-empty assistant message, falling back to a recap of tool names).
ops.quote: last non-empty assistant message → recap of tool names

ops.text: Because Ollama often ignores `response_format` and ends a job on a silent tool call, `run_agent` sends a one-shot "reply now in plain text, no more tools" nudge when a job finished its required writes but left no prose and no `structured_response`, so `agent_runs.result` is a real summary.
ops.quote: reply now in plain text, no more tools

ops.text: Before this design, one LLM client per role was kept alive for the life of the process (days, in a long-running container); a long-lived Ollama connection would eventually go stale and wedge further requests, sometimes affecting Ollama access elsewhere on the machine.
ops.quote: sometimes badly enough to affect Ollama access from elsewhere on the machine

ops.text: Every LLM/MCP connection the codebase opens has a bounded lifetime of one request or one scheduled job, and any new call site must keep that invariant.
ops.quote: if you add a new call site, keep that invariant

ops.text: The role `.md` prompt files hold only standing behaviour (identity, lane/boundaries, the standard method); everything job-specific lives in `app/jobs.py`'s `SCHEDULED_REQUESTS`, each a self-contained `PURPOSE:` line followed by numbered steps, and new job detail should stay out of the `.md` files.
ops.quote: Keep new job detail out of the `.md` files

ops.text: `system.md` has no "you are X" identity claim, since every role gets it appended before its own role fragment.
ops.quote: no "you are X" identity claim

ops.text: `app/prompts.system_prompt_for(role, settings)` prepends a one-line `current_context_block` (current date/time in `settings.tz`) that mainly points the model at `get_job_context`.
ops.quote: prepends a one-line `current_context_block`

ops.text: `get_job_context` is built per run in `app/job_context.py`, appended by `run_agent`, and closes over `settings` and the `job_name` that `run_job` threads down.
ops.quote: built per run in `app/job_context.py`

ops.text: `get_job_context` returns date math in which every reference date carries its weekday name, plus the intent behind a scheduled run (`JOB_CONTEXT` gives each job a `focus`/`rationale` and a `menu_scope`).
ops.quote: every reference date carries its weekday name

ops.text: `build_job_context` resolves `menu_scope` into `job.target_menu_days`, the exact `weekly_menu` weekday rows the job acts on, because that table is keyed by weekday not date and the model must not do date-to-weekday arithmetic itself.
ops.quote: the model must not do date→weekday arithmetic itself

ops.text: The cron day/time is deliberately never surfaced to the model, since a job can be `/invoke`d at any time.
ops.quote: The cron day/time is deliberately never surfaced

ops.text: Interactive chat gets `run_type: "interactive_chat"` and `job: null` in its job context.
ops.quote: `run_type: "interactive_chat"`, `job: null`

ops.text: `zoneinfo` needs the `tzdata` package on Windows, pinned in `requirements.txt` for `sys_platform == "win32"` (Linux/Docker has it from the OS).
ops.quote: pinned in `requirements.txt` for `sys_platform == "win32"`

ops.text: `app/models.py` holds the structured `response_format` models: `SousChefResult` and `PantryManagerResult` are wired per role in `RESPONSE_FORMATS` (for both chat and jobs).
ops.quote: wired per-role in `RESPONSE_FORMATS`

ops.text: `ExecutiveChefResult` is not in `RESPONSE_FORMATS`, so chat with the chef stays free text; it is passed to `run_agent(response_format=...)` only by the `weekly_menu` job (`JOB_RESULT_MODELS`).
ops.quote: is passed to `run_agent(response_format=...)` only by the `weekly_menu` job

ops.text: `app/jobs.py` holds `SCHEDULED_REQUESTS` (canned scheduled prompts), the `JOB_ROLES` / `JOB_RESULT_MODELS` / `JOB_REQUIRED_TOOLS` / `JOB_REQUIRED_TOOL_COUNTS` maps, and `run_job()`, which passes them to `run_agent`.
ops.quote: `JOB_ROLES` / `JOB_RESULT_MODELS` / `JOB_REQUIRED_TOOLS` / `JOB_REQUIRED_TOOL_COUNTS` map set

ops.text: Scheduled job prompts are deliberately silent on which day/time they normally run, since `/invoke/{job_name}` can fire any of them at any time.
ops.quote: deliberately silent on which day/time they normally run

ops.text: `run_agent` compares the tool calls actually made against `require_tools` (each must appear at least once) and `require_tool_counts` (each must appear at least N times; `weekly_menu` needs 28 `add_weekly_menu_item` calls).
ops.quote: must appear ≥ N times

ops.text: On a shortfall, `run_agent` sends up to `_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` corrective "still outstanding: ..., do it now" turns and then raises.
ops.quote: up to `_MAX_FOLLOWUPS` corrective

ops.text: Chat history is not kept in process memory: `run_agent()` loads and saves each session's message list from/to dbmcp's `chat_sessions` table (`app/history.py`) using `langchain_core.messages.messages_to_dict`/`messages_from_dict`.
ops.quote: Chat history is not kept in process memory

ops.text: Scheduled jobs call `run_agent(..., remember=False)`, which skips chat history entirely so each scheduled run is a fresh one-shot request.
ops.quote: each scheduled run is a fresh one-shot request

ops.text: `agents/app/server.py` is the single deployable unit that replaced the old `agent-worker` container; its FastAPI `lifespan` starts an `AsyncIOScheduler` (`app/scheduler.py`) that calls `run_job()` in-process, the same way the HTTP route does.
ops.quote: replaces the old `agent-worker` container

ops.text: agent-api exposes `POST /chat`, `POST /invoke/{job_name}`, `GET /jobs` and `GET /health`.
ops.quote: `GET /jobs`, and `GET /health`

ops.text: `POST /chat` is keyed by session id with a per-session `asyncio.Lock`, so only same-session turns serialize.
ops.quote: only same-session turns serialize

ops.text: `cli.py` is a separate, unrelated entry point: a standalone terminal REPL over `run_agent()` for local dev with no server or scheduler.
ops.quote: a separate, unrelated entry point

ops.text: There is no per-role tool allowlist (`app/mcp_tools.load_tools()` takes no role argument); this deliberately simplified the previous `ROLE_TOOLS` filtering, and per-role restriction is easy to reintroduce if a role misuses a tool.
ops.quote: easy to reintroduce per-role tool restriction later

ops.text: `run_job` must always pass `trace=False`: `trace=True` returns a human-readable event transcript, not JSON, and passing it silently broke sous_chef/pantry_manager job telemetry for a while.
ops.quote: **Always pass `trace=False` from `run_job`**

ops.text: The `result_model.model_validate(...)` check on a job's structured output is intentionally non-fatal (logs a warning, doesn't raise), because Ollama's `create_agent(..., response_format=...)` support is flaky and the tool calls/DB writes have already happened, so a validation miss must never turn a real success into a reported failure.
ops.quote: intentionally non-fatal

ops.text: A noncompliant weekly plan can reach the household and be acted on same-day: the `weekly_menu` job still emails the plan and `nightly_prep` still creates prep tasks before the first audit pass (Saturday 10:00 plan, Saturday 20:00 prep, Saturday 22:30 audit), and it is caught only after the fact via score/feedback, never blocked.
ops.quote: caught only after the fact via score/feedback, never blocked

ops.text: This lack of a synchronous gate was accepted deliberately in favour of one rule source (the Food Inspector's LLM-as-judge scoring) rather than a second deterministic checker that would need syncing as restrictions become configurable.
ops.quote: Accepted deliberately in favor of one rule source

ops.text: `validate_weekly_menu_policy` and its backing `menu_policy_violations` / `RESTRICTED_LUNCH_TERMS` were removed outright, not deprecated.
ops.quote: removed outright, not deprecated

ops.text: `run_job` posts run telemetry to dbmcp's `/api/agent-runs` (`app/telemetry.py`) regardless of success or failure.
ops.quote: regardless of success/failure

ops.text: `chatui/app.py` has no LangChain/MCP dependency and imports nothing from `agents`.
ops.quote: does not import anything from `agents`

ops.text: chatui's `/api/chat` and `/api/automations/*` proxy to agent-api (`AGENT_API_URL`, default `http://agent-api:8090`) the same way `/api/dashboard` etc. proxy to dbmcp (`DB_API_URL`).
ops.quote: exactly the way `/api/dashboard` etc. proxy to `dbmcp`

ops.text: Being a pure REST client let chatui's Docker image drop the shared root `requirements.txt` and build from its own directory with just `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `httpx` and `pydantic`.
ops.quote: with just `fastapi`/`uvicorn`/`httpx`/`pydantic`

ops.text: chatui's inventory-mutation proxies (`PATCH /api/inventory/{id}`, `.../discard`) are commented out (no caller) now that the Pantry page is read-only.
ops.quote: are commented out (no caller)

ops.text: `App.jsx` holds `page` in `useState` and switch-renders `Dashboard`/`Pantry`/`WeeklyMenu`/`Recipes`/`TaskList`/`Chat`/`Automations`/`UsageStats`/`Profile`.
ops.quote: holds `page` in `useState`

ops.text: All pages except `Recipes`, `Automations` and `UsageStats` are fed from one `/api/dashboard` payload fetched on mount and patched locally after each mutation.
ops.quote: fed from one `/api/dashboard` payload fetched on mount

ops.text: `Automations` fetches its own data from `/api/automations/jobs` and `/api/automations/runs` and can trigger `/api/automations/invoke/{job_name}` to show a job's output without waiting for its cron time.
ops.quote: fetches its own data from `/api/automations/jobs` and `/api/automations/runs`

ops.text: `Recipes` calls `search_recipes`/`rate_recipe`/`delete_recipe` (via `/api/recipes*`) directly rather than reading the dashboard payload.
ops.quote: directly rather than reading the dashboard payload

ops.text: The Recipes page's "refresh tags"/"rewrite instructions" buttons post a one-off request straight to `/api/chat`.
ops.quote: post a one-off request straight to `/api/chat`

ops.text: `UsageStats` reads `/api/usage-stats/daily` and `/api/usage-stats/breakdown`, which chatui proxies to dbmcp's `/api/agent-runs/usage-summary` and `/api/agent-runs/usage-breakdown`.
ops.quote: chatui proxies to dbmcp's `/api/agent-runs/usage-summary`

ops.text: `UsageStats` renders `agent_runs.context_length`/`input_tokens`/`output_tokens`/`total_tokens` as daily totals for the last 7 days and all-time min/max/avg overall and per `agent_role`.
ops.quote: daily totals for the last 7 days

ops.text: `Profile` reads/writes the single `user_profile` row via `/api/profile` (also embedded in the dashboard payload as `profile`) and does CRUD for `household_members` via `/api/household-members`.
ops.quote: reads/writes the single `user_profile` row via `/api/profile`

ops.text: The dashboard payload carries a `constants` block (`days`, `meal_types` and their order maps) so the React app never hard-codes the weekday/meal vocabulary; `WeeklyMenu.jsx` builds its grid from `data.constants`.
ops.quote: so the React app never hard-codes the weekday/meal vocabulary

ops.text: `WeeklyMenu`, `TaskList` and `Recipes` each render a `score`/`audit_feedback` badge per row, showing "Unaudited" when `score` is `null`.
ops.quote: ("Unaudited" when `score` is `null`)

ops.text: `Chat.jsx` can list and switch back into recent conversations via `GET /api/chat-sessions` (proxied to dbmcp's `GET /api/chat-sessions?limit=5`) and `GET /api/chat-sessions/{id}`.
ops.quote: `Chat.jsx` can list and switch back into recent conversations

ops.text: dbmcp's chat-session listing returns the 5 most recently updated sessions ordered by `updated_at`, with a preview built from the first human message; it does not prune anything, only limits what is returned.
ops.quote: it doesn't prune anything, it only limits what's *returned*

ops.text: For `GET /api/chat-sessions/{id}`, chatui converts dbmcp's raw LangChain-dict messages into the simple `{role, content}` shape the UI renders, dropping tool-call and empty-content messages.
ops.quote: dropping tool-call/empty-content messages

ops.text: Picking a past conversation swaps the browser's stored `session_id` and repopulates the transcript; agent-api's history load/save is unaffected.
ops.quote: swaps the browser's stored `session_id` and repopulates the transcript

ops.text: CLAUDE.md's chatui section says the Profile `email` is where dbmcp sends the "new prep task" notification, but the same file says email lives entirely in agent-api and dbmcp has no SMTP or notification routes; the dbmcp wording is presumed stale and needs confirmation.
ops.quote: its `email` is where dbmcp sends the "new prep task" notification
